blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — facility emergency action and fire safety
stem: Which element is required in a workplace emergency action plan under OSHA 29 CFR 1910.38?

options.A: Procedures for reporting emergencies, evacuation and exit-route assignments, accounting for employees, and designated rescue or medical duties.
options.B: A requirement that staff remain at their workstations until an outside emergency agency arrives and gives individualized evacuation instructions.
options.C: A policy that evacuation-route information be limited to supervisors so movement can be directed centrally during a fire or other emergency.
options.D: A plan to silence employee alarms during drills and emergencies so warning signals do not disrupt patient care or routine workplace operations.

rationale: A is correct. OSHA 29 CFR 1910.38(c) requires emergency-action plans to include procedures for reporting fires or other emergencies, emergency evacuation and exit-route assignments, accounting for employees after evacuation, rescue and medical duties for designated employees, and other specified elements. B and C conflict with evacuation planning and employee access to the plan. D conflicts with OSHA's requirement to maintain an employee alarm system with distinctive signals.
educational_objective: Recognize core OSHA emergency-action-plan elements: emergency reporting, evacuation/exit routes, employee accountability, and assigned rescue or medical duties when applicable.

option_audit.A: Correct; matches multiple minimum elements explicitly listed in 1910.38(c).
option_audit.B: Plausible command-and-control error but inconsistent with planned evacuation procedures.
option_audit.C: Plausible centralized-control error but inconsistent with plan availability and employee training/review requirements.
option_audit.D: Plausible disruption-avoidance error but conflicts with the required employee alarm system.

cueing_audit.answer_length: All options are comparable in structure and detail; the key is not uniquely signaled by length.
cueing_audit.absolute_words: No distractor relies on a simplistic all/only/never/always cue.
